slot.brief: Products and structures on hydrolysis of PCl5 / SiCl4 / NCl3 with balanced outcomes; ask which hydrolysis gives a specific oxide acid set — high-difficulty, multi-product reasoning.

stem: On complete hydrolysis in excess water, which set gives the balanced equations for $\text{PCl}_5$, $\text{SiCl}_4$, and $\text{NCl}_3$, respectively?

verdicts.working: Complete hydrolysis gives H₃PO₄ and HCl from PCl₅, SiO₂ and HCl from SiCl₄, and NH₃ and HClO from NCl₃. These balanced equations are all in (A).

working:
$\text{PCl}_5+4\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4+5\text{HCl}$; $\text{SiCl}_4+2\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{SiO}_2+4\text{HCl}$; $\text{NCl}_3+3\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{NH}_3+3\text{HClO}$.

Independent check: Complete hydrolysis gives H₃PO₄ and HCl from PCl₅, SiO₂ and HCl from SiCl₄, and NH₃ and HClO from NCl₃. These balanced equations are all in (A).
solution:
Complete hydrolysis of $\text{PCl}_5$ and $\text{SiCl}_4$ gives phosphoric acid and silica, respectively; $\text{NCl}_3$ hydrolyses to ammonia and hypochlorous acid.
$$\text{PCl}_5+4\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4+5\text{HCl},\quad \text{SiCl}_4+2\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{SiO}_2+4\text{HCl}$$
$$\text{NCl}_3+3\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{NH}_3+3\text{HClO}$$
These equations correspond to (D).

draft.distractor_notes: B: Gives the partial hydrolysis product POCl₃. C: Incorrectly changes P(V) to phosphorous acid and adds oxygen. D: Gives an intermediate partial hydrolysis product of NCl₃.
